title: CHW Diabetes Self-Management Support
recommendation_text: Conduct monthly home visits to provide culturally tailored diabetes education, medication adherence support, and blood glucose monitoring guidance. Connect patients to community resources for nutrition and physical activity programs.
implementation_guidance: Schedule 60-90 minute monthly visits using validated DSMES curriculum. Provide blood glucose meter training and supplies. Create personalized action plans with patients. Maintain updated directory of local food assistance and exercise programs.
expected_outcomes: 0.5-1.0% reduction in HbA1c levels (95% CI: 0.3-1.2%), improved medication adherence >80%, increased self-monitoring frequency, 22% reduction in diabetes-related hospitalizations. Number needed to treat (NNT): 8 patients to prevent one hospitalization.
citation_title: Diabetes Management: Interventions Engaging Community Health Workers

title: Doula Prenatal Support
recommendation_text: Provide minimum 4 prenatal visits offering childbirth education, emotional support, birth plan development, and healthcare system navigation. Focus on culturally competent care and patient advocacy throughout pregnancy.
implementation_guidance: Schedule initial visit by 28 weeks gestation. Conduct 2-3 additional prenatal visits (60-90 minutes each). Develop personalized birth plan with patient preferences. Coordinate with prenatal care providers. Provide 24/7 on-call availability starting at 37 weeks.
expected_outcomes: 53% reduction in cesarean delivery rates (95% CI: 42-64%), 57% reduction in postpartum depression/anxiety diagnosis, increased breastfeeding initiation rates, higher maternal satisfaction scores. NNT: 6 patients to prevent one cesarean delivery.
citation_authors: Falconi AM, Bromfield N, Felder JN, Elder J, Giurgescu C
citation_title: The effect of doula care on birth outcomes in Medicaid populations: A systematic review

title: Nurse Hypertension Management
recommendation_text: Lead multidisciplinary hypertension management team using standardized medication titration protocols, lifestyle counseling, and regular follow-up monitoring. Coordinate care with pharmacists, CHWs, and dietitians.
implementation_guidance: Implement evidence-based protocols for BP management using collaborative practice agreements. Schedule structured follow-up visits every 2-4 weeks until BP goal achieved. Use electronic health records for population health monitoring and outreach.
expected_outcomes: 70-80% of patients achieve BP goal (<130/80 mmHg) compared to 30-40% with usual care (95% CI: 35-45% improvement), reduced clinical inertia in medication management, improved provider efficiency. NNT: 3 patients to achieve one additional BP control.
citation_title: Cardiovascular Disease: Team-Based Care to Improve Blood Pressure Control
cost_effectiveness: Cost savings of $2,500-$4,000 per patient annually

title: Pharmacist Medication Therapy Management
recommendation_text: Conduct quarterly comprehensive medication reviews for patients with diabetes taking multiple medications, focusing on adherence barriers, drug interactions, and therapy optimization. Provide medication action plans and communicate recommendations to primary care providers.
implementation_guidance: Schedule 45-60 minute initial consultations followed by 20-30 minute quarterly follow-ups. Use standardized documentation templates for medication reviews. Implement collaborative practice agreements for medication adjustments. Provide direct patient education on proper medication use.
expected_outcomes: 0.8% mean reduction in HbA1c (95% CI: 0.5-1.1%), 35% improvement in medication adherence rates, 42% reduction in medication-related problems. NNT: 12 patients to prevent one diabetes-related emergency department visit.
citation_authors: Jeong S, Patel I, Hata M, Arnall J, Hwang W, Jones C, Choi Y
citation_title: Clinical and economic outcomes of pharmacist-led medication therapy management for patients with type 2 diabetes: A systematic review and meta-analysis
citation_journal: Research in Social and Administrative Pharmacy
target_population: Adults with type 2 diabetes on multiple medications
cost_effectiveness: Return on investment of $3.30 for every $1 spent

title: CHW Blood Pressure Self-Monitoring
recommendation_text: Implement home blood pressure monitoring program with bi-weekly CHW support visits to validate technique, review readings, and provide lifestyle modification coaching. Establish clear protocols for when patients should contact healthcare providers based on BP thresholds.
implementation_guidance: Provide validated home BP monitors and train patients on proper measurement technique. Create standardized BP log templates. Schedule bi-weekly 30-minute home visits for first month, then monthly for 5 months. Develop referral pathways for readings above threshold values.
expected_outcomes: 11.7 mmHg greater reduction in systolic BP compared to usual care (95% CI: 8.2-15.2 mmHg), 5.4 mmHg greater reduction in diastolic BP (95% CI: 3.1-7.7 mmHg). NNT: 6 patients to achieve one additional controlled BP.
citation_authors: Margolis KL, Asche SE, Dehmer SP, Bergdall AR, Green BB, Sperl-Hillen JM, et al.
citation_title: Long-term outcomes of the effects of home blood pressure telemonitoring and pharmacist management on blood pressure among adults with uncontrolled hypertension: Follow-up of a cluster randomized clinical trial

title: Behavioral Health Depression Screening
recommendation_text: Implement systematic depression screening using PHQ-9 for all adult patients, with integrated behavioral health follow-up within 7 days for positive screens. Establish warm handoff protocols between primary care and behavioral health services.
implementation_guidance: Train all clinical staff on PHQ-9 administration and scoring. Create EHR templates for documentation and tracking. Develop workflow for same-day behavioral health consultations when possible. Establish registry for tracking patients with positive screens.
expected_outcomes: Increased depression identification by 27% (95% CI: 19-35%), 62% of patients with moderate-to-severe depression showing clinically significant improvement at 6 months. NNT: 5 patients screened to identify one case of previously undiagnosed depression.
citation_title: Screening for Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: US Preventive Services Task Force Recommendation Statement
target_population: All adults, especially those with risk factors

title: Peer Support Substance Use Recovery
recommendation_text: Provide weekly peer recovery support services for individuals with substance use disorders, focusing on recovery planning, resource navigation, and social support. Integrate peer support with clinical treatment services and community resources.
implementation_guidance: Schedule initial 90-minute assessment to develop personalized recovery plan. Conduct weekly 60-minute individual or group sessions. Train peers in motivational interviewing and CCAR Recovery Coach model. Implement standardized documentation system for recovery goals and progress.
expected_outcomes: 47% reduction in substance use (95% CI: 38-56%), 42% improvement in treatment retention, 35% reduction in emergency department visits. NNT: 4 patients to prevent one treatment dropout.
citation_authors: Eddie D, Hoffman L, Vilsaint C, Abry A, Bergman B, Hoeppner B, et al.
citation_title: Lived Experience in New Models of Care for Substance Use Disorder: A Systematic Review of Peer Recovery Support Services and Recovery Coaching
cost_effectiveness: Cost savings of $2,400 per patient annually in healthcare utilization

title: Care Coordinator Chronic Disease Management
recommendation_text: Implement nurse-led care coordination program with monthly patient contact to address care gaps, coordinate specialist appointments, and provide self-management support. Utilize risk stratification to identify high-need patients for more intensive intervention.
implementation_guidance: Develop risk stratification algorithm using clinical and social determinants data. Create care coordination documentation templates. Schedule monthly 30-minute check-ins via phone or video. Establish communication protocols with primary care and specialty providers.
expected_outcomes: 23% reduction in all-cause hospitalizations (95% CI: 17-29%), 32% reduction in emergency department visits, 18% improvement in medication adherence. NNT: 9 patients to prevent one hospitalization.
citation_title: Effectiveness of Nurse-Led Case Management in Cancer Care: Systematic Review
cost_effectiveness: Return on investment of $1.80 per $1 spent

title: Social Worker Housing Intervention
recommendation_text: Provide comprehensive housing case management services for patients experiencing housing instability, including assessment, housing navigation, application assistance, and landlord mediation. Coordinate with community housing resources and legal aid services.
implementation_guidance: Conduct standardized housing instability assessment at intake. Create directory of local housing resources and eligibility requirements. Schedule weekly 45-60 minute case management sessions until housing is secured. Develop follow-up protocol for 6 months post-housing placement.
expected_outcomes: 73% of clients secure stable housing within 6 months (95% CI: 65-81%), 48% reduction in emergency department visits, 52% reduction in inpatient hospitalizations. NNT: 2 clients to achieve one stable housing placement.
citation_authors: Aubry T, Bloch G, Brcic V, Saad A, Magwood O, Abdalla T, et al.
citation_title: Effectiveness of permanent supportive housing and income assistance interventions for homeless individuals in high-income countries: A systematic review
cost_effectiveness: Net savings of $6,300 per person in healthcare and social service costs

title: PCP Prediabetes Intervention
recommendation_text: Implement intensive lifestyle intervention program for patients with prediabetes, including structured diet and physical activity guidance, with quarterly monitoring of glycemic status. Refer eligible patients to CDC-recognized Diabetes Prevention Programs.
implementation_guidance: Screen all eligible patients for prediabetes using ADA risk assessment. Provide initial 30-minute counseling session on lifestyle modifications. Schedule quarterly follow-up visits for monitoring. Develop referral pathway to local DPP programs.
expected_outcomes: 58% reduction in progression to type 2 diabetes (95% CI: 48-66%), mean weight loss of 5-7% of initial body weight, improvements in cardiovascular risk factors. NNT: 7 patients to prevent one case of diabetes over 3 years.
citation_authors: Haw JS, Galaviz KI, Straus AN, Kowalski AJ, Magee MJ, Weber MB, et al.
citation_title: Long-term Sustainability of Diabetes Prevention Approaches: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials

title: Doula Postpartum Support
recommendation_text: Provide 3-5 postpartum home visits within the first 6 weeks after birth to support breastfeeding, maternal recovery, newborn care, and mental health screening. Implement structured assessment for postpartum depression at each visit.
implementation_guidance: Schedule first visit within 3-5 days of birth. Conduct Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale screening at 2 weeks and 6 weeks postpartum. Provide hands-on breastfeeding support and education. Develop referral pathways for lactation specialists and mental health providers.
expected_outcomes: 62% increase in breastfeeding continuation at 6 weeks (95% CI: 53-71%), 44% reduction in postpartum depression diagnosis, improved maternal confidence scores. NNT: 5 mothers to prevent one case of breastfeeding discontinuation.
citation_authors: Kozhimannil KB, Hardeman RR, Attanasio LB, Blauer-Peterson C, O'Brien M
citation_title: Doula care, birth outcomes, and costs among Medicaid beneficiaries
cost_effectiveness: Cost savings of $1,200 per birth in reduced complications and readmissions

title: Nurse Cardiovascular Risk Reduction
recommendation_text: Implement nurse-led cardiovascular risk reduction program with monthly visits focusing on medication adherence, lifestyle modification, and self-monitoring of key parameters. Utilize motivational interviewing techniques to address barriers to behavior change.
implementation_guidance: Calculate 10-year ASCVD risk score at baseline. Develop personalized risk reduction plans. Schedule monthly 45-minute visits for 6 months, then quarterly. Create patient-friendly tools for tracking BP, physical activity, and dietary patterns.
expected_outcomes: 27% reduction in cardiovascular events over 5 years (95% CI: 18-36%), mean systolic BP reduction of 8.6 mmHg, 18% reduction in LDL cholesterol. NNT: 21 patients to prevent one cardiovascular event over 5 years.
citation_authors: Uthman OA, Hartley L, Rees K, Taylor F, Ebrahim S, Clarke A
citation_title: Multiple risk factor interventions for primary prevention of cardiovascular disease in low- and middle-income countries
target_population: Adults with multiple cardiovascular risk factors

title: Behavioral Health Pain Management
recommendation_text: Deliver 8-session cognitive behavioral therapy program for chronic pain management, focusing on pain coping strategies, activity pacing, and addressing catastrophizing thoughts. Incorporate mindfulness techniques and graduated physical activity.
implementation_guidance: Conduct comprehensive pain assessment using validated tools (Brief Pain Inventory, PEG scale). Develop structured 8-session CBT protocol with weekly 50-minute sessions. Create patient workbook with home practice exercises. Train providers in pain-focused CBT techniques.
expected_outcomes: 30% reduction in pain intensity (95% CI: 22-38%), 45% improvement in functional status, 40% reduction in pain catastrophizing. NNT: 4 patients to achieve clinically significant pain reduction.
citation_authors: Williams ACC, Fisher E, Hearn L, Eccleston C
citation_title: Psychological therapies for the management of chronic pain (excluding headache) in adults

title: CHW Prenatal Care Coordination
recommendation_text: Implement CHW-led prenatal care coordination program with monthly home visits to address social determinants of health, provide education, and ensure attendance at prenatal appointments. Focus on high-risk pregnancies and individuals with barriers to care.
implementation_guidance: Develop standardized prenatal education curriculum. Schedule monthly 60-minute home visits throughout pregnancy. Create screening tool for social needs assessment. Establish referral pathways for food, housing, transportation, and other resources.
expected_outcomes: 63% reduction in missed prenatal appointments (95% CI: 52-74%), 42% reduction in low birth weight deliveries, 37% increase in breastfeeding initiation. NNT: 8 pregnancies to prevent one low birth weight delivery.
citation_authors: Cunningham SD, Lewis JB, Thomas JL, Grilo SA, Ickovics JR
citation_title: Expect With Me: development and evaluation design for an innovative model of group prenatal care to improve perinatal outcomes
cost_effectiveness: Cost savings of $1,450 per pregnancy in reduced complications

title: Pharmacist Medication Reconciliation
recommendation_text: Implement pharmacist-led medication reconciliation within 72 hours of hospital discharge for patients with cardiovascular conditions. Conduct comprehensive review of all medications, resolve discrepancies, and provide patient education on new regimens.
implementation_guidance: Schedule 45-60 minute post-discharge medication review. Develop standardized reconciliation documentation template. Create patient-friendly medication schedules with visual aids. Establish communication protocol with hospital and primary care teams.
expected_outcomes: 67% reduction in medication discrepancies (95% CI: 58-76%), 42% reduction in 30-day readmissions, 53% improvement in medication adherence at 3 months. NNT: 12 patients to prevent one 30-day readmission.
citation_authors: Mekonnen AB, McLachlan AJ, Brien JA
citation_title: Effectiveness of pharmacist-led medication reconciliation programmes on clinical outcomes at hospital transitions: a systematic review and meta-analysis
target_population: Adults discharged from hospital with cardiovascular conditions
cost_effectiveness: Return on investment of $5.10 per $1 spent
